title: Ayin Hebrew Letter (ע): Sound, Pronunciation & Words
description: Learn the Hebrew letter Ayin (ע): why it usually adds no consonant sound in modern Israeli Hebrew, like Aleph, plus words like עַיִן (eye) and practice.

blocks.0: Ayin Hebrew Letter (ע): Sound, Words & Practice
blocks.9: The Hebrew word 'עוּגָה' [u-ga] means 'cake'. It consists of four letters: Ayin (ע), Vav (ו), Gimel (ג), and Hey (ה). In the pronunciation taught here, Ayin adds no separate consonant sound. Shuruk (וּ), Vav with a dot inside, represents [u], with no separate [v]. Gimel with Kamatz Gadol gives [ga]. Hey (ה) at the end of the word has no separate [h] sound here. Read [u-ga] in two syllables, with stress on ga.
blocks.11: Read each word aloud. In the exercises, you will also review נָא [na], 'please', often used in formal requests and on signs, and נַחַל [na-khal], 'stream' or 'brook', with stress on na. Here kh represents one consonant sound, like the 'ch' in Scottish 'loch' or German 'Bach', not the English 'ch' in 'chair'.

4.tip: עַיִן is the Hebrew word for 'eye'.

theory.heading: Meet Ayin
theory.intro: The sixteenth letter of the Hebrew alphabet. In the common modern Israeli pronunciation taught here, Ayin usually adds no consonant sound of its own, just like Aleph (א): you pronounce the vowel written with it. Some speakers, especially in Mizrahi Hebrew, pronounce it deep in the throat. Its name, עַיִן, is also the Hebrew word for “eye.”
objectives: Read Ayin with the vowel written with it, and know the other pronunciations you may hear.
Read Ayin in real words like <bdi class="hebrew" lang="he" dir="rtl">עַיִן</bdi> (eye) and <bdi class="hebrew" lang="he" dir="rtl">עוּגָה</bdi> (cake).

examples.heading: Ayin in real words
examples.intro: Read three words with Ayin and see how each one is pronounced, then read five more words aloud for reading practice.
